claims.text: Greg Short asserts that early-stage entrepreneurs who focus on profitability optimization or delegation of tasks to free up their time are over-optimizing for the wrong stage of business; this behavior indicates they are taking strategic advice from operators running much larger companies, advice that does not apply to zero-to-early-revenue contexts.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Early-stage entrepreneur (pre-scale, low or no revenue)
Founder is personally the primary customer-contact and delivery vehicle
claims.mechanism: Profitability and delegation concerns are legitimate constraints at scale, but at the early stage the binding constraint is customer acquisition and relationship density, not operational efficiency; optimizing for the wrong constraint delays revenue generation.
bounded_by: Does not apply to founders who have already achieved significant scale and have genuine operational bandwidth problems

claims.text: Greg Short contends that in the early stage of building a business, the correct strategy is to do deliberately unscalable high-touch work — specifically spending all available hours doing direct customer outreach (e.g., DMing customers manually) — because this is what every successful operator did before they had scale.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: No existing customer base or revenue system in place
claims.mechanism: High-touch unscalable work at early stage builds the customer relationships and revenue base needed to eventually justify scalable systems; skipping this phase leaves no economic foundation to optimize.
bounded_by: Not applicable once revenue and customer base are sufficient to justify systematization

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that direct, personal customer outreach via DMs — done at high enough volume to cause physical strain (he used a Bluetooth keyboard attached to his phone to avoid thumb arthritis) — is a legitimate and necessary early-stage customer acquisition method, not an embarrassing workaround.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Early-stage business with no automated lead generation
Founder is primary or sole customer-contact

examples.text: Greg Short describes attaching a Bluetooth keyboard to his iPhone because he was DMing customers so frequently that his thumbs risked developing arthritis. This illustrates his claim that unscalable, high-volume direct customer outreach is the correct early-stage behavior — the discomfort was a signal of doing the right thing at the right volume, not a problem to be optimized away.

practices.text: If you are an early-stage entrepreneur, spend all available extra hours doing direct customer outreach (DMs, calls) rather than attempting to systematize or delegate; optimization comes after the economic foundation exists.
